lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Coffee Roasters | Barista | Metro City, USA | Oct 2025 - Present
- Prepared drinks for the morning rush of about 200 orders and kept the bar stocked.
- Opened the café three days a week and handled the daily cash count.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Migrated 40 department sites to a shared component library, cutting new-page build time from 2 days to half a day.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; my findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Writes the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybook, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Make sure the code URL leads directly to a useful portfolio or code profile.
items.because: A generic landing page would be less useful.

items.says: Confirm that “Expected Jun 2026” is still accurate when submitting the résumé.
Consider placing engineering experience ahead of the barista role.
items.because: The engineering experience is more relevant to frontend applications.

items.says: Clarify whether you personally prepared 200 orders or the team handled that volume.
Fix the “cafØ” character-encoding error.
Consider cutting the cash-count bullet if space is tight.
items.because: It is less relevant than the engineering work.

items.says: Name the performance metric and how it was measured.
items.because: “Page performance” is too broad to evaluate.

items.says: Specify the audit’s scope if it covered only the date picker.
items.because: “All” could sound like a claim about the whole product.

items.says: Verify that the three regressions were caught by those tests before release.
Correct or remove the claim that lazy-loading the hero image cut LCP.
items.because: Lazy-loading an above-the-fold hero commonly worsens LCP.

items.says: Remove or correct the XSS-prevention claim.
items.because: React state does not sanitize input, and dangerouslySetInnerHTML bypasses React’s normal escaping.

items.says: Verify that the load-time and A/B-test figures are attributable to this work.
Check that the build-time comparison uses the same kind of page before and after.
Check that the drop in broken-page reports was measured over comparable periods.
Change “Writes” to past tense.
Clarify your contribution to the checklist if others maintained or approved it.
Identify what “search time” measures.
items.because: It could mean response time or a person’s time finding a course.

items.says: Link directly to the live app or repository if available.
Be prepared to explain how weekly usage was measured.
Check that both timings came from comparable slow-3G tests.
Ensure the transit agency’s link is still live.
Check the two-month date range.
items.because: It may prompt questions for a hackathon project.

items.says: Resolve the heading’s Vue claim against the first bullet’s React and TypeScript claim.
Specify your frontend contribution more precisely.
items.because: This is the least distinctive project bullet unless the calendar bullet covers all of the contribution.

items.says: Remove the travel-search bullet from the library-booking project.
items.because: It appears to duplicate the Lumen achievement and does not fit the hackathon.

items.says: Group the listed skills more accurately than under “Tools.”
items.because: TypeScript is a language, while React, Vue, and Angular are frameworks or libraries.

items.says: Keep Angular only if you can discuss hands-on experience with it.
Consider whether the Methods section adds information beyond the bullets.
items.because: The space could be used for stronger evidence if the résumé runs long.
